name: Emergence
one_line: Enterprise platform of agents over company data, composed of Assess and Enrich modules (Toolkit planned), with solutions for Data Insights (talk-to-data), Data Governance and Semiconductor analytics; exposes a hosted MCP server that outside agents can call, and uses A2A between its own agents.

gamma_ray.fact_ray: 25 facts: 25 π Moderate. Each is written beside its evidence above.
gamma_ray.built_from: Emergence AI's own public pages (product, documentation, blog, customer stories, legal and security pages)

configs.what: The Semiconductor solution, a separate set of services deployed on CRAFT
Deployments that include the Data Insights (Talk2Data) solution, per the MCP page
Agent audit turned on for a project, per the audit log page

facts.label: It works across several domains or systems
facts.fact: The data connections page lists implemented connections to PostgreSQL, Redshift and Snowflake databases, S3, GCS and MinIO storage and NFS file systems; the release notes (2026.04) say the Snowflake connector serves cataloging, profiling and natural-language querying alongside PostgreSQL and Redshift sources.
facts.quote: configured links to external data sources: databases, object storage, and file systems

facts.label: The agent works independently; the person approves critical decisions only
facts.fact: The release notes (2026.03) say the DQ execution, DQ assessment and metadata assessment workflows no longer require approval because they are read-only analyses, while DQ tag and rule generation still require approval; the Data Governance workflows page (captured) says a person's approval (Save) of a profiling or enrichment run is what applies its changes to the scorecard.
facts.quote: results are available immediately on completion, since these are read-only analyses

facts.label: There is a published protocol or communication layer between agents
facts.fact: The agents talk to each other over the published A2A protocol, with Agent Cards for discovery.
facts.quote: All inter-agent communication uses the A2A protocol

facts.label: It exposes an agent interface: a published MCP server, an agent card, or an API documented for agents to call
facts.fact: The documentation publishes a hosted MCP server that outside agents and IDE clients can call, with OAuth 2.0 PKCE; the endpoint did not answer our read-only probe.
facts.quote: external agents to CRAFT's tool gateway over the Model Context Protocol

facts.label: It asks for narrower access than the whole account
facts.fact: The MCP page says the X-Project-ID header selects a project but grants no access, that project membership is checked server side against the caller's token, and that each project keeps an allowlist of the tools each agent identity may call, refusing others with tool_not_allowed; execute_query accepts SELECT statements only, and only this page states the allowlist as current.
facts.quote: project membership is enforced server-side against your JWT's claims

facts.label: High-impact actions need a person's approval
facts.fact: The release notes (2026.03) say generated data quality tags and rules are previewed, with their SQL and validation status, and a reviewer approves them before they are persisted.

facts.label: What it can reach is enumerated: scopes, permissions, tools
facts.fact: The admin guide lists project roles (Owner, Admin, Developer, Operator, Viewer) and what each may do; the MCP page also lists the tools by name.
facts.quote: Read resources and trigger workflows. Cannot create or delete resources.

facts.label: Its limits and known failure cases are documented for those who use it
facts.fact: The MCP page has an errors and limits table, including a 500-row cap on query results and SELECT-only queries.

facts.label: The data it uses is described
facts.fact: The security docs describe four classification levels for the data the platform processes and the handling for each.
facts.quote: CRAFT classifies all data processed by the platform into defined sensitivity levels

facts.label: The models and third-party components it uses are listed
facts.fact: The introduction names the third-party components (Keycloak, OpenFGA, Prefect, LiteLLM) and says models are reached through LiteLLM, naming Gemini, GPT and Claude in an open list.
facts.quote: via LiteLLM (Gemini, GPT, Claude, and more)

help.label: Our hypothesis, not their claim. Built from public pages only; nothing of theirs was tested.
help.pitch: RiskMandate would measure, for one real deployment of Emergence's agents, what each agent was asked to do (its mandate), what its credentials and connections actually let it reach (its grant), and the difference between the two (the gap), and keep that as a written record. It is read-only: never in the request path.

items.title: Check and claim the GAMMA-Ray card
items.text: The card is beta and read only from public pages; Emergence has not reviewed it. A correction is dated and published, and a file at /.well-known/fact-ray.json on their own domain raises the trust of every fact on it.

items.title: Measure one deployment
items.text: Pick one agent in one deployment; RiskMandate records its mandate, its grant and the gap, read-only. The lens page explains the measurement.

items.text: The same task run bare and under one policy, with the probes and the record public, as in our own harness runs (simulated data only).
